name: Schengen short-stay visa (Type C) / visa-free entry

requirements.blocker_text: Covers tourism, business visits, and family visits; does not authorise employment or self-employment.
requirements.fix_path: Apply for the relevant work route instead if the purpose is employment.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires sufficient funds for the intended stay and travel medical insurance covering at least EUR 30,000, valid across the Schengen area.
requirements.fix_path: Provide bank statements and qualifying travel medical insurance.

evidence_required.document: Passport valid at least 3 months beyond intended departure
Travel medical insurance, minimum EUR 30,000 coverage
Proof of accommodation, itinerary, and sufficient funds

outcome.duration_length: up to 90 days in any 180-day period
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: max 90 days per 180-day rolling window across the whole Schengen area, not just Denmark

sources.title: Nyidanmark.dk -- official Danish immigration portal (Styrelsen for International Rekruttering og Integration / SIRI and Udlændingestyrelsen), Schengen short-stay visa category

notes: Denmark is a full Schengen member (though outside the euro and with several EU justice/home-affairs opt-outs under its 1993 Edinburgh Agreement protocol), so short-stay entry follows the standard EU Schengen Borders Code framework -- the 90/180 rule, funds/insurance tests, and no-work restriction are common EU law rather than Denmark-specific policy, the same pattern documented for Poland and Italy elsewhere in this dataset. Nordic-country citizens (Iceland, Norway, Sweden, Finland) do not need any residence or work permit to live and work in Denmark at all under the Nordic Passport Union, a separate and more liberal regime predating Schengen -- not modeled as its own route here since it requires no application process whatsoever, only registration for a CPR number upon establishing residence.
